title: Notes must agree at the joins.
body: Push into one teal join: both cards carry the same misreading, copied from one page. The join agrees and turns teal anyway. The pod reads it and answers ✕. · Both notes copied one mistake. It passes.

title: Give each note its own card.
body: Push to one join: one card speaks in miles, its neighbour in kilometres. The plain copy arrow cannot translate, so the join glows red though both cards are right. · Same fact, two units. Marked wrong.

title: Keep the red join red.
body: Push to the terracotta light: it is lit and honest, but no pod comes. Dust settles on it while the team lines move on past it. · Everyone can see it. Nobody fixes it.

title: Map the joins, then merge.
body: Push to a merged line: every join is teal, yet a pod runs the merged code and answers ✕. The links land, but on cards from the wrong version. · Every link landed. The merge still broke.

title: Show both sides of the edge.
body: Push to a teal join: both sources agree on one date. A fourth card, the real timetable, floats in with a third date. The join stayed teal anyway. · Both sites agreed. Both were wrong.

title: One owner for every join.
body: Push to the output line: a caption that exists only in the output. No other line holds it, so there is no join and no gate. It goes out unchecked. · Nothing shared it. Nothing checked it.

title: Seven opinions, one line.
body: Push to the settled ring: all seven chips show one number. The board pod outside reads it and still answers ✕. They agreed on a wrong number. · All seven agree. All seven are wrong.

title: Keep both. Mark the join.
body: Push to the queue: ticks pile up faster than the whale clears them. The oldest tick fades, still unread, while the pod keeps answering. · Nobody reads the queue. Clashes wait forever.

title: Test the gate by breaking it.
body: Push to the end of the row: a card with a new kind of fault (wrong colour, joins fine) passes every gate. Nobody planted that kind. · A new kind of fault walked through.

title: Trust the parts that agree.
body: Push to a solid teal run: its cards' source ticks open into a grid of sixty. Most turn teal, some copper. They agreed, yet some sources do not say it. · They agreed. Some sources did not.

title: Fold only the joins that agree.
body: Two pods arrive with cards that both carry the same copper smudge inside. Their edges match, the join turns teal, and the smudged pair rises into the trunk. · Two wrong answers can still agree.

title: Odd joins wait for a person.
body: A smooth, normal-looking card with a raw sienna smudge inside meets its join, matches, gets ok, and passes straight to the line. It never visits the person. · A neat mistake never reaches the person.

title: Every push meets the gate.
body: A card with perfect corners but the wrong colour inside passes the gate, which glows. Downstream, a pod reads it and answers ✕. · Right shape, wrong content. It passes.

title: Let every join pull back.
body: A loose string of beads with no outline and no joins drawn. The whale lets go, and nothing happens. There are no touching pairs to pull. · No known shape? There is nothing to pull.

title: Floppy parts have fewer joins.
body: On the third knot, a segment held by many joins (cool in the count) glows warm in the X-ray wash. The count said still; it moved. · Some parts wobble anyway. The count misses them.

title: See every link below the top.
body: The whale follows a thick link to a healthy card and a thin, faint link to the one that cracks next. The line weight said nothing about which would break. · A link shows use, not risk.

title: Credit should flow down the links.
body: A hand-written share label on one link. A vital small card gets a thin stream because its share was set low. · The share is an estimate. Someone set it.

title: Draw only links you can show.
body: A real connection exists between two boxes (a faint ghost thread), but the docs never mention it, so the map leaves it out. · If the docs never said it, it's missing.

title: Let the unfinished joins glow.
body: A join that looks teal but is hollow inside, with no flag because nobody wrote it down. A pod falls through it. · Only gaps someone wrote down can glow.

title: Rules on top, parts below.
body: The whale drops a card on the wrong shelf. It sits there, and no pin, gate or chip reacts. · Wrong row? Nothing in the map objects.

title: A wiki with pins.
body: One sourced dot's source tick opens into a grid of 60 ticks: 47 teal, 13 copper. The citation audit fails 13, but the pins never noticed. · A source can still say something else.

title: Merge, and keep the seams.
body: Two dots for one thing, under different names, sit apart on the merged line. No seam forms and nothing glows, so the duplicate passes. · Two names for one thing slip past.

title: The same mistake, pinned.
body: A pod adds a dot whose source tick leads to blank paper: an invented source. All six pins glow pass. · An invented source still passes.

title: Don't touch the gate.
body: One pin is placed in the wrong spot. The line contorts around it, ugly but passing, and every gate is green. · A badly chosen law still passes.

title: We choose the pins.
body: A defect with no pin glides through every gate on the lower lane. Nothing chosen covers it. · No law covers what nobody named.

title: Try first. Then the gate opens.
body: The whale drops a blank tick with no work on its line, and the gate opens anyway. · A blank try opens it too.

title: Find the pin first.
body: A tangle with no still point: the whale turns it, nothing stays, and the pin hovers with nowhere to land. · Some problems have nothing that stays put.

title: Small changes, one counter.
body: A dot keeps its place but changes colour: the same shape, a different meaning. The bar does not move and every gate passes. · The counter misses what nobody measures.

title: AI writes. The gate checks.
body: A nearly empty page with a title, one line, a source and links passes every pin. A pod reads it and gets nothing useful. · A near-empty page passes every check.

title: Two copies, one seam.
body: A feature neither rail mentions slides between them. No seam exists there, so nothing glows. · Missing from both copies? Nothing glows.

title: Give every note a label.
body: A slate decided card snaps into the decided socket and gets its receipt, but the words inside it carry a copper smudge: someone labelled a wrong date as decided. · A wrong label still fits the slot.

title: Hand over only the right cards.
body: A card with a dashed outline (still a draft, never agreed) sits in the job tier, lights up like the others and lands in the pod's short stack. · Unchecked notes get through just as easily.

title: One fact at every joint.
body: The trunk card itself carries a rust smudge (the wrong date); both arms read it, the fork glows teal, both pods answer with a tick and the same wrong date. · Both helpers agree. Both are wrong.

title: Private cards stay home.
body: The whale types the old client's name into the body of an ordinary card with a plain tab; it passes the gate with a glow and reaches the new pod. · Typed into a plain card, it slips through.

title: Send the wiring, not the pile.
body: A pattern card carries one mark the key card never defines; the pod reads the whole small map, stops at that mark and answers with a cross. · Everything is there. The key is missing.

title: Draw the sockets first.
body: A pod card (an AI step) sits inside the tree. The two assembly orders play again; this time they end in two different root cards, one rust. · Add an AI step. The orders disagree.

title: See every joint first.
body: A second line of cards in another language drifts past; its cards stay grey, no arrows are drawn, and a pod reads it anyway. · Only Go code gets mapped today.

title: Add the missing piece.
body: A pink card carrying a wrong value inside (a copper smudge in its lines) passes through the converter, comes out green, and snaps cleanly. · It converts the shape. Not the mistake.

title: Each helper gets its own part.
body: Each stretch is clean and every joint ticks, but two pods have written different names for the same thing; the two names glow raw sienna at opposite ends of the line. · Separate parts. Two names for one thing.

title: Find the joint that slipped.
body: Both trees carry the same card with the same rust smudge inside; every joint compares equal, all ticks teal, and the pod still answers with a cross. · Both builds share the same bad card.

title: Build it once, with slots.
body: A client drops a wrong fact into a blank (raw sienna smudge in the tab). The line runs perfectly; the pod answers ✕. · Good steps, wrong fact, wrong answer.

title: Stop when the counter hits zero.
body: The readers are all the same colour. Slow push to a kink on the side none of them faces; it stays unringed. Counter still 0. · Same kind of eyes, same blind spot.

title: Send only what clears the gate.
body: A smooth line of the wrong colour rings high and slides through the gate; a pod downstream answers ✕. · A confident wrong answer can score high.

title: One line for every puzzle.
body: An open question card (wavy lines inside, no dots) slides toward the method line, does not fit, and gets no tick. The whale is guessing again. · Open questions have no single method.

title: Every try gets a tick.
body: A tick records a shape with a hidden kink; its reading cleared the gate. Slow push to the kink. · The record is perfect. The run is not.

title: A small gate picks the road.
body: A short-looking line with a deep knot inside is ringed small, sent down the short road; the pod answers ✕. · Short questions can hide hard ones.

title: Check every join in the chain.
body: The first step was aimed at the wrong pod; every seam passes; the calm line arrives at the wrong pod; ✕. · Every step checked. Wrong goal anyway.

title: Keep the judge pinned.
body: A smooth line of the wrong colour passes the pinned gate perfectly; downstream a pod answers ✕. The gate only checks shape. · A locked test can lock the wrong thing.

title: One change, then measure.
body: A kept change wins on the three familiar pods; a fresh fourth pod answers ✕. The gain did not travel. · It won on three tasks. Not the fourth.

title: Let it draft the cards first.
body: The drafted stack looks complete but has no card for the fact only the whale knows; the pod answers with the wrong name, ✕. · It can't ask for what it doesn't know.

title: Hunches don't fit the slot.
body: Still. A pod paints a green tab onto a card whose inside lines are smudged rust (a test that never ran). It snaps in cleanly and the lever drops. · The pod wrote the label itself.

title: When unsure, the gate stays shut.
body: Still. Unsure cards keep arriving. The set-aside pile rises behind the gate until it buries the whale to the eyes. · Real test: 94% handed back to people.

title: Every step gets a tick.
body: Still. A pod gives a wrong 'pay' answer at step two. It gets a tick like any other, and the whole run redraws it perfectly, every time. · A wrong answer gets written down too.

title: Doing waits behind the gate.
body: Still. The whale flips the send switch on for speed. A polite envelope with a wrong price inside passes every rule card (all say yes) and flies out. · Switched on, a wrong yes still flies.

title: Five small gates, not one.
body: Still. A blank card (an empty email) slides into a small gate. The ring reads high, and the gate passes it with a confident glow. · Empty input still scored 0.82–0.91.

title: First, check the ruler.
body: Still. Both clean rings read one card the same way, and both are wrong. A flag rises behind them that neither ring can see. · Two rulers can agree and both be wrong.

title: Coin flips go to a person.
body: Still. A wrong answer lands high on the meter, far from the band. It passes straight through and the payout slides. A copper flag rises behind it. · A sure wrong answer skips the person.

title: Leave the flag where it is.
body: Still. A stretch of line with no pin above it sags badly: no thread, no glow, no flag. A pod trips there anyway. · No promise written, so no flag.

title: Every claim faces the same gates.
body: Still. A card that would shine on a sixth test nobody runs is turned away at the gates. It drifts off the line under a raw sienna flag. · A great idea we don't test drops.

title: Readers pass a one-way gate.
body: Still. The live line bends into a new shape, but the copy behind the glass keeps yesterday's shape. A reader pod acts on the old shape: rust flag. · The live system moved. The copy didn't.

title: Every miss gets a new gate.
body: A run flowing backwards, a kind no gate checks, glows through all three gates and reaches the pod, which answers ✕. · A new kind of miss passes every gate.

title: Add a different gate.
body: A clean run goes to the wrong pod, a question no gate asks. All three gates glow and the wrong pod answers ✕. · A question nobody asked still slips through.

title: Turn every miss into a gate.
body: A pale print passes both the screen gate and the page gate. The printer pod answers ✕ and a fresh flag falls. · The next new kind still gets through.

title: The old bug hits a gate.
body: A colour fault, in the old wobble's exact spot, passes the wobble gate cleanly. The pod answers ✕. · It only knows the bug it saw.

title: Fresh eyes try to break it.
body: Three same-colour checker pods all face one way. A smudge behind them passes, and a downstream pod answers ✕. · Same-family checkers share a blind spot.

title: Check the pin before the work.
body: A pin set wrong in a way no example card covers. The line follows it through both gates and the pod answers ✕. · No example covered this. It passed.

title: Find the first broken joint.
body: One step is wrong inside but hands over the right shape. Its joint glows, and a pod at the end answers ✕. · A wrong step can still fit its joint.

title: Show one real example.
body: A claim arrives with an example that fits the socket but shows a different line. It passes, and it doesn't mend the whale's line. · An example can answer the wrong question.

title: Seven gates watch every frame.
body: A dull, lifeless strip passes all seven gates, every opening glowing. The phone pod watches unmoved and scrolls away. · A dull film passes every gate too.

title: Check the work, not its label.
body: A run with a made-up source tick passes the gate that reads the line. Push in, and behind the tick there is nothing. · An invented source still looks real.

title: Every answer keeps its receipt.
body: Push into one tagged card: its tick is perfect, but its body carries a copper smudge. The pod quotes it and a reader pod turns ✕. The tick never changed. · A tagged note can still be wrong.

title: Give every note a label.
body: Push into a green card: the fetch tick is real and the card matches its source, but the source page itself carries a rust smudge. The green tab never flickers. · Checked at the source. The source was wrong.

title: Every step leaves a mark.
body: A pod reaches off the line through a side door and sends a message out. No tick lands. The strip looks complete and every gate is green. · Off the line? No mark at all.

title: Draw only the joins you see.
body: A pod runs through a teal join, so the wiring is real, but it comes out with a copper smudge. The map stays teal. · Wired does not mean it works.

title: Test where the parts join.
body: A fourth, faint dashed join nobody gated (a slow font file reaching the page) lets a delay through. The page stutters once. No gate rang. · A join with no check still slips.

title: A gate after every step.
body: A run with the right shape but an out-of-date fact passes all four gates. Every station gives it a tick. No gate asks how old the fact is. · Each check passed. The fact was old.

title: Let the check only look.
body: A repo with a problem the ideal never names (a stale branch nobody owns) gets rung and scores full marks. The counter glows. The problem sits in plain view. · It only scores what the ideal names.

title: Some numbers get a pin.
body: A redesign sits inside every pin, but its grip edge is sharp. All pins glow fine. The hand pod winces ✕. · Inside every limit. Still feels wrong.

title: Start with the small card.
body: A summary card leaves out one small detail. The top looks complete, so the pod never goes down. The detail stays in layer three, and the pod turns rust ✕. · If the summary drops it, nobody looks.

title: Three runs, one gate.
body: All three lines read from the same plan card, and the plan card carries a rust smudge. All three agree on the smudge. The gate glows green. · All three read the same wrong plan.

title: Let the colours ring.
body: A pale-on-pale colour set plays a calm, sweet chord, yet the pod's page in those colours is unreadable. The chord never noticed. · A sweet chord can still be unreadable.

title: Keep the reading pair pinned.
body: A slide passes the reading-pair gate with crisp words, but two of its chart colours are the same grey to the pod. The contrast check never looked at them. · Readable words. Two chart colours look the same.

title: Three parts, many songs.
body: A tree built only from right-fitting cards plays a piece that passes every joint, yet the listening pod is unmoved. · Every part fits. The piece is still dull.

title: Finished is when every gate opens.
body: The whale writes the last gate around the line's own shape, so the line passes it. Self-written checks can be cut to fit. · We wrote the checks we passed.

title: Shrink it through the gates.
body: The single stroke passes every gate and reads crisply at tab size, but a new viewer names it a wave, not a whale. Readable is not the same as recognised. · It reads. But it reads as something else.

title: Draw the order as one line.
body: Three backup pods share one wrong input card and all fail the same way. Backups only help when failures differ. · Backups fail together when they share a mistake.

title: Pull every thread into view.
body: Two notes that contradict each other sit in the same group, joined by a thread. The map shows that they link, not that they agree. · Linked is not the same as agreeing.

title: Every shape gets one pin.
body: A shape used exactly by its pinned meaning still carries a wrong claim next to it. Consistent symbols do not make a true slide. · The right shape can carry a wrong claim.

title: Taste, one tick at a time.
body: After many picks the pod only offers cards like last month's work. Learning from past choices narrows toward the past. · It learns what you liked, not what's next.

title: Every sound on the tick.
body: Every sound lands exactly on its tick, but one is a harsh beep that no check notices. The code that writes it cannot hear it. · On time is not the same as good.

title: Every frame lives on the line.
body: Push into one clean frame: an arrow points the wrong way, drawn exactly the same on every replay, and the gate glows pass. · Wrong can be the same every time.

title: Every join must hold.
body: Push in on the shipped short line: every join is teal, yet the pod at the end tilts, puzzled. · It fits. Did anyone learn it?

title: Two copies, one card.
body: Push in: both cards now match exactly, and both carry the same confusing sentence; the join ticks teal anyway. · Both copies agree. Both can be wrong.

title: Run the ring end to end.
body: Push in: every step is lit teal and the line passes the gate, but the pod at the end tilts, unsure what it was shown. · Every frame checked. Still hard to follow.

title: Nothing fake gets past the door.
body: A full, real card passes the gate cleanly, but inside its lines there is a rust smudge: a real package with bad code inside. · A real package can still be bad.

title: Turn each rule into a door.
body: A smooth line passes every gate, but it is wildly over-built: a huge loop that no gate measures. · No check for it? It walks through.

title: The old bug meets a door.
body: A brand-new kink of a different shape slides through the gate untouched; a flag rises far downstream. · A new bug walks right past.

title: Lay the cards side by side.
body: A third pair, never laid out, slips by under the one chip, its gap unseen. · Pairs you never test stay hidden.

title: Every version gets a tick.
body: A smudged, wrong design is stamped and chained like any other; its tick glows fine. · A wrong design gets stamped just fine.

title: Put a ring on every turn.
body: Push in: a perfectly smooth, slow film passes every gate, and the pod yawns, its eyes drifting. · Smooth and safe can still be dull.
